correctness.rationale: After gauge normalization, signed incidence cycles correspond bijectively to interior arrays whose negative-position entries sum to zero. Positive entries are killed by balanced corner squares. Negative entries are linked by balanced same-row/column squares, or by a balanced four-negative/positive-corner square after positive elimination; any two negative entries therefore differ by a generated vector. This proves exact kernel equality and the dimension dichotomy for every m,n>=2. The regular signed-cover two-path relations realize each balanced square as a boundary. Exact finite checks: 606 signing/rank cases and 94 independently assembled cover-path cases; finite checks corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: This is an all-parameter structural spanning theorem for a natural signed graph family, with an exact dimension loss under arbitrary frustration. It establishes that real degree-one signed GLMY homology is blind to all choices of edge signing on dense triangle-free bicliques, even though the unbalanced signed double cover may retain ordinary cycles. The generative connectivity lemma is not a single numerical invariant or a merely negative normalization check.
